thinking_and_logic: You began with a nested-loops brute-force plan, then recognized it would be too slow for up to 1e5 elements. With hints, you moved to the standard invariant: as you scan left-to-right, maintain a hash map from previously seen value to its index. At each index i, compute complement = target - nums[i] and if it's already in the map, return the stored index and i; otherwise store nums[i]. This ensures you never reuse the same element and correctly handles duplicates.
code_assessment: Your final code essentially matches the answer key's optimal solution (single pass + hash map; check complement before inserting). Compared to other common approaches, you avoided sorting (which complicates index recovery) and avoided the 'same element twice' bug by looking only at prior indices. Functionally and asymptotically it achieves what the canonical solution targets: O(n) expected time and O(n) space with robust handling of duplicate values.
